mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when this trigger is met.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% indicates weakening consumer demand, which reduces corporate revenue growth expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in at least 70% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly unemployment rate below 5% for four consecutive months signals a tight labor market, which increases wage pressures and input costs, ultimately compressing profit margins and resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly different from zero in these episodes (t-test p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline of more than 1% in the industrial production index (INDPRO) signals contraction in manufacturing activity, reducing corporate earnings expectations and leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered months.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in unemployment rate (UNRATE) and a fall in payroll employment (PAYEMS) by more than 0.5% in the same month signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate profits, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE rises and PAYEMS falls by >0.5% in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative in at least 70% of such co-movement episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent decline in both real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) and housing starts (HOUST) by more than 1% month-over-month indicates a broad-based collapse in demand, which depresses corporate earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 and HOUST both decline >1% month-over-month
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of such co-movement episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate held constant at or below 0.5% for six consecutive months in a low-inflation environment signals accommodative monetary policy, which supports risk asset valuations and produces positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS ≤ 0.5% for six consecutive months and CPIAUCSL < 2%
regime_hint: zero lower bound with low inflation
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly above zero in at least 70% of such episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly increase of at least 0.5% in the industrial production index (INDPRO) for four consecutive months signals an expansion in manufacturing output, which boosts corporate earnings and leads to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO rises by ≥0.5% for four consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive in at least 70% of such episodes.
